title: Ostrogothic Kingdom
capsule: The Ostrogothic Kingdom of Italy (officially Regnum Italiae) was established by Theoderic the Great, who invaded in 489 at the behest of Byzantine Emperor Zeno and, after besieging Ravenna, defeated and killed the Germanic ruler Odoacer in 493, making Ravenna his capital. Theoderic governed a dual polity — Romans retained civil administration under Roman law while Goths held military command — fostering three decades of stability and the patronage of Boethius and Cassiodorus; at its widest extent the kingdom encompassed Italy, Sicily, Dalmatia, Provence, and nominally Pannonia. After Theoderic's death in 526, succession disputes and religious friction with Constantinople gave Justinian I a pretext to invade in 535; the Gothic War devastated the Italian peninsula over two decades, with a Gothic resurgence under Totila extinguished only when Byzantine general Narses defeated the last Ostrogothic king Teia at Mons Lactarius in 553.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Ostrogothic core in Italy is thoroughly documented in Roman senatorial sources, papal records, Cassiodorus's Variae, and Byzantine chronicles; frontier extent in Dalmatia, Provence, and Pannonia is well attested but underwent rapid change during the Gothic War.
